row.evidence: Twingate's pricing page lists "User provisioning & management via IdP" and "SSO via Okta, Entra ID, and more" under Business ($10 per user per month), and the Okta, Entra ID and JumpCloud SCIM integrations are checked only for Business and Enterprise.
row.notes: SCIM (Okta, Entra ID, OneLogin, JumpCloud) starts at Business, $10/user/mo on the page's yearly view, versus Teams at $5. Google Workspace sign-in plus Directory-API user and group sync is on every plan including free Starter (Twingate-run, not SCIM); it is treated as Google sign-in, not SAML/OIDC SSO, so sso_plan is Business. Twingate documents its SCIM 2.0 endpoint but says it is not meant for self-serve use, so idp.generic is true with that caveat. Disabled users keep counting toward billing. The GraphQL Admin API (all plans, including Starter) can create, disable and delete users. Monthly prices are about 15% higher; the comparison table's monthly view shows $12 for both Teams and Business, which looks like a page error.

auth.notes: Docs call it a long-lived bearer token; no expiry is stated, so "never" means long-lived until replaced.

deprovision.notes: Okta deactivation deactivates the Twingate user; SCIM DELETE deletes the user. The offboarding guide says users disabled in the Admin Console keep counting towards billable users, but it does not say whether an IdP deactivation via SCIM is billed the same way (c31).

filtering.notes: Entra mapping marks externalId as supported for filtering; sorting is not supported.

attributes.notes: Twingate documents the last name as name.lastName; the Entra gallery mapping uses name.familyName and emails[type eq "work"].value.

rate_limits.text: 25 requests per second per Twingate account

limitations.text: No /.search, /Bulk or /Me endpoints, and no sorting on filter queries.
SCIM endpoints are documented only to support the existing IdP integrations, not for self-serve use.
Users synced from an IdP cannot be modified in the Twingate Admin Console.

scim.notes: Twingate documents the SCIM API but says the endpoints are for its supported IdP integrations (Okta, Entra ID, OneLogin, JumpCloud), not for self-serve use. Each IdP integration must first be connected for sign-in (OIDC/SAML) before SCIM is configured.

auth.notes: X-API-KEY header; tokens are generated under Settings > API with one of three permission levels and optional IP allow-ranges.

capabilities.notes: userDetailsUpdate takes state ACTIVE or DISABLED, which covers deactivate and reactivate.

endpoints.purpose: users query (list users) / user query (get one user)
groupUpdate mutation (add/remove users and resources); groupCreate, groupDelete

audit_log_api.notes: Audit logs are exported from the Admin Console or synced to S3 (c42); no audit-log query appears in the GraphQL schema.

rate_limits.text: 60 reads and 20 writes per minute per account by default; 429 when exceeded

okta.notes: OIDC sign-in plus SCIM; needs Okta Lifecycle Management for SCIM.

google.notes: Twingate-run sync over the Google Workspace Directory API; all plans.

onelogin.notes: From Twingate's own OneLogin guide; OneLogin catalogue page not loaded.

fallbacks.other_sync: Google Workspace Directory API user and group sync (all plans)
fallbacks.notes: Users are created at first sign-in when Okta is used without Lifecycle Management, or when Entra assignment is not required (both OIDC).

conflicts.text: The pricing page cards show Teams $5 and Business $10 per user per month in the yearly view ("Yearly -15%"), while llms.txt lists the same prices with "15% discount billed yearly", implying they are monthly list prices. The pricing page is used.

open_questions: Docs do not say whether a SCIM deactivation stops billing for the user (Admin Console disabled users still count).
Whether SCIM deactivation ends active client sessions is not documented.
No audit-log API is documented; audit logs are console export or S3 sync only.
Custom SCIM attributes and enterprise-extension attributes are not documented.
